whyItMatters: This is one of the highest-fidelity CodeBuild abuse patterns: an execution-changing build launch is followed by sensitive credential or secret activity soon afterward.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may inject a malicious build launch and then use the build runtime or build role to access secrets, assume roles, decrypt protected data, or create new credentials.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is attractive because it turns a trusted CI/CD path into a short-lived privileged execution environment.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The ordered combination of risky launch override plus sensitive follow-on activity is much stronger than either event alone.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, defenders may fail to connect build-path manipulation to the sensitive cloud actions it enabled.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for CodeBuild
AWS CloudTrail management events for IAM, STS, Secrets Manager, and KMS
loggingRequirements: Override-backed StartBuild events and follow-on sensitive events must be ingested into the same analytics environment.
The detector should link the initiating actor to build-role activity where possible.
The engine must support ordered time-window correlation.
limitations: Direct actor-only joins may miss sensitive actions executed solely by the build role.
Some legitimate builds intentionally access secrets or decrypt data.
The model is strongest when project-role lineage is available.

enrichment.description: Resolve the project service role and any derived execution identity used after launch.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Improves correlation between launch and follow-on sensitive actions.

enrichment.description: Classify the post-build action as secrets access, role assumption, decrypt, or credential creation.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Makes the abuse path easier to triage.

enrichment.description: Assess whether the launch override could plausibly drive the later sensitive activity.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Raises confidence that the two stages are causally linked.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should model a CodeBuild abuse chain: a build is started with execution-changing overrides and sensitive cloud activity follows soon afterward from the same initiating context or linked build role. It should require event order and stable linkage across the two stages.
conditions: first eventSource equals codebuild.amazonaws.com and eventName equals StartBuild with buildspecOverride or environmentVariablesOverride present
second event is GetSecretValue, CreateAccessKey, AssumeRole, or Decrypt by the same normalized actor or linked build execution identity
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Require order. 2. Link initiator and build role where possible. 3. Escalate strongly when the project is privileged or the override content clearly enables the follow-on activity.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when an override-backed build launch is followed quickly by sensitive credential, secrets, or decryption activity.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium with build-role lineage and ordered correlation

deployment.scheduling: Near-real-time is preferred because the override-to-sensitive-activity chain is immediately actionable.
considerations: This is the highest-fidelity CodeBuild credential-theft detector in the batch.
Build-role lineage and override content context are the main dependencies.
